title: Cofinality of coherent vertices of a directed cover by simplicial cones
statement: Use the universes, simplicial sets, quasicategories, ordinary nerves, coherent cocones and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $L$, its right cone $L^{\triangleright}=L\star\Delta^0$ consists of the simplices of $L$, the simplices at a new vertex, and the ordered concatenations of a simplex of $L$ with simplices at that new vertex. Let $K$ be a small quasicategory, let $A$ be a small nonempty partially ordered set in which every finite subset has an upper bound, and let $(K_a)_{a\in A}$ be simplicial subsets with $K_a\subseteq K_b$ for $a\leq b$ and $K=\bigcup_a K_a$. Suppose each $K_a$ is equipped with a simplicial isomorphism $L_a^{\triangleright}\cong K_a$ for some small simplicial set $L_a$; denote its cone vertex by $t_a$. The subsets $K_a$ need not be quasicategories. There exists a simplicial map $j:N(A)\to K$ with $j(a)=t_a$ such that $j$ is cofinal in the following explicit sense: for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, coherent diagram $H:K\to\mathcal E$ and coherent cocone on $H$, that cocone is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $j$ is colimiting. The comparison uses the same cocone vertex and the restricted legs, and is natural in $H$. No existence of all small colimits in $K$ or $\mathcal E$ is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384: retraction onto K for a directed family of subsets with final vertices; the right-cone special case. The construction uses Proposition 4.2.3.4, Proposition 4.2.3.8, Remark 4.2.3.9 and Proposition 4.1.1.8. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this coherent result.

proof.text: For each $a$, use its given identification $K_a\cong L_a\star\Delta^0$. Define the augmented operation $c_a:(K_a)_m\to(K_a)_{m+1}$, also for $m=-1$ with the unique empty simplex, by appending one vertex $t_a$: in the join normal form retain the entire $L_a$-part and lengthen the final constant $t_a$-block by one. In particular $c_a(\varnothing)=t_a$. Restriction of ordered blocks gives $d_{m+1}c_a\sigma=\sigma$, $d_ic_a\sigma=c_ad_i\sigma$ for $i\leq m$, $s_ic_a\sigma=c_as_i\sigma$ for $i\leq m$, and $c_ac_a\sigma=s_{m+1}c_a\sigma$. Thus appending a repeated last cone vertex is a degeneracy. These are direct identities of the join normal forms, including the pure cone simplices. They define a simplicial map $\rho_a:K_a^{\triangleright}\to K_a$: fix the base and replace every new cone vertex by an appended $t_a$. The edge from the old $t_a$ to the new cone vertex maps to $\operatorname{id}_{t_a}$.

source.place: Right-cone special case of the retraction in the proof of Proposition 5.3.1.16, pp. 383-384; explicit join normal forms.

proof.text: Form $K_F$ with the degreewise disjoint-union and operator rules in [lem-coef-directed-decomposition-right-anodyne], using $I=A$. Equivalently it is the construction in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones] for the ordinary functor $a\mapsto(K_a\hookrightarrow K)$: a compatible family of lifts of a lower simplex is uniquely its membership in the first subset, because all transition maps are inclusions. In particular it contains $K$ and $N(A)$, and there is a canonical map $\iota_a:K_a^{\triangleright}\to K_F$ with constant upper chain at $a$. Its sets of simplices are small, being small unions of products of the given small sets. Only the definitions of the two displayed constructions are used here.

Define $r:K_F\to K$ as the identity on the pure $K$-simplices. For a mixed simplex with lower simplex $\sigma\in(K_{a_{i+1}})_i$ and chain $a_{i+1}\leq\cdots\leq a_n$, set $r(\sigma;a_{i+1},\ldots,a_n)=c_{a_n}\cdots c_{a_{i+1}}\sigma$, viewing each intermediate simplex in the next subset by inclusion. For a pure nerve simplex use the same formula starting with the empty lower simplex: $r(a_0\leq\cdots\leq a_n)=c_{a_n}\cdots c_{a_0}(\varnothing)$. Each intermediate value lies in the subset indexed by its last index. A face deleting a lower vertex commutes through all the $c_a$ by $d_ic_a=c_ad_i$. A face deleting an upper vertex commutes through the later operations until it reaches $d_{m+1}c_a=\operatorname{id}$, removing that operation; this also handles the first upper index and a disappearing block. A lower degeneracy commutes through the $c_a$, and repeating an upper index is exactly $c_ac_a=s_{m+1}c_a$. Pure-block cases are the same identities with the empty block allowed. Hence all faces and degeneracies commute with $r$. No compatibility of the different cone identifications beyond the subset inclusions is used. We have $r|_K=\operatorname{id}$ and $r\iota_a=\rho_a$. Set $j=r|_{N(A)}$; the empty-simplex formula gives $j(a)=t_a$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.3.1.16, pp. 383-384, construction of r and j; explicit formula for the given right-cone structures.

proof.text: Fix a quasicategory $\mathcal E$ and $H:K\to\mathcal E$. Every local cocone $H\rho_a$ on $H|_{K_a}$ is colimiting, as follows. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cone-mono-right-anodyne] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow L_a$: its coned map is $\{t_a\}\hookrightarrow K_a$, so it is right anodyne even though $K_a$ need not be a quasicategory. By [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], for every $T\in\mathcal E$ restriction is an equivalence $e_T:\operatorname{Coc}_{K_a}(H|_{K_a},T)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H(t_a),T)$, where $\operatorname{Coc}_B(p,T)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_BT)$. Let $b_T$ send a map $H(t_a)\to T$ to its postcomposition with $H\rho_a$. The component of $H\rho_a$ at $t_a$ is the identity by step 1, so $e_Tb_T$ is homotopic to the identity on the whole mapping space. Thus $b_T$ is an equivalence. The dual mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says exactly that $H\rho_a$ is colimiting. The join cocone is interpreted as a transformation using the ordered map $K_a\times\Delta^1\to K_a^{\triangleright}$ specified in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones].

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4 local colimit hypothesis; normalized cone at the final vertex in the proof of Proposition 5.3.1.16. Cone/right-anodyne tools as stated in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Put $q=Hr:K_F\to\mathcal E$. Its restriction to $K$ is $H$, and $q\iota_a=H\rho_a$ is colimiting by step 4. Apply [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones] to the small category $A$, its subset functor and this specific extension $q$. It gives equivalences $R_T:\operatorname{Coc}_{K_F}(q,T)\to\operatorname{Coc}_K(H,T)$, given by actual restriction, natural in $T$ and compatible with postcomposition. Only the displayed local colimits are needed; no other colimits in $\mathcal E$ are assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4, last assertion, pp. 249-250; applied to q=Hr.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-coef-directed-decomposition-right-anodyne] hold: $A$ is small and nonempty, has upper bounds for finite subsets, and its increasing family covers $K$ in every simplicial degree. Consequently $N(A)\hookrightarrow K_F$ is right anodyne. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] with $B=K_F$, $A=N(A)$, and diagram $q=Hr$. This gives restriction equivalences $S_T:\operatorname{Coc}_{K_F}(q,T)\to\operatorname{Coc}_{N(A)}(Hj,T)$, natural in $T$ and compatible with postcomposition. This application permits arbitrary simplicial sets as indexing shapes, so it does not assume $K_F$ is a quasicategory.

Precomposition with $r$ gives $r^*_T:\operatorname{Coc}_K(H,T)\to\operatorname{Coc}_{K_F}(Hr,T)$. Since $r|_K=\operatorname{id}_K$, the composite $R_Tr^*_T$ is the identity. The equivalence $R_T$ from step 5 therefore makes $r^*_T$ an equivalence. The composite $S_Tr^*_T$ is precisely restriction $j^*_T$, because $r|_{N(A)}=j$. Hence $j^*_T:\operatorname{Coc}_K(H,T)\to\operatorname{Coc}_{N(A)}(Hj,T)$ is an equivalence for every $T$. These maps are actual precomposition functors on the entire simplicial mapping spaces. They commute with restriction in $H$ and with postcomposition in $T$, so the equivalence is natural in $H$ as well.

source.place: The retraction argument concluding Proposition 5.3.1.16, p. 384; composition of the two restriction comparisons.

proof.text: Let $\lambda$ be any cocone on $H$ with apex $x$. For each $T$, the two maps out of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,T)$ given by postcomposition with $\lambda$ and with $j^*\lambda$ form a commuting triangle whose third map is the equivalence $j^*_T$ of step 7. Thus one map out of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,T)$ is an equivalence if and only if the other is. By the dual mapping-space criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\lambda$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction is. Restriction retains the apex $x$ and every specified leg along $j$; it is natural in $H$ as checked in step 7. This proves the assertion without assuming existence of any other colimits in either $K$ or $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.1.8 and the conclusion of Proposition 5.3.1.16; universal property of the given cocone.

lean.statement: theorem exists_cofinal_of_directed_cone_cover (K : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory K] (A : Type u) [PartialOrder A] [Nonempty A] (hA : ∀ s : Finset A, ∃ b : A, ∀ a ∈ s, a ≤ b) (B : A → K.Subcomplex) (hB : Monotone B) (hcover : iSup B = ⊤) (L : A → SSet.{u}) (e : ∀ a : A, orderedJoinFunctor.obj (L a, Δ[0]) ≅ (B a).toSSet) : ∃ j : nerve A ⟶ K, (∀ a : A, j.app (op ⦋0⦌) (ComposableArrows.mk₀ a) = (B a).ι.app (op ⦋0⦌) ((e a).hom.app (op ⦋0⦌) ((orderedJoinInr (L a) Δ[0]).app (op ⦋0⦌) (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm 0)))) ∧ ∀ (E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (H : K ⟶ E) (c : (coconeCategory H) _⦋0⦌), IsColimiting H c ↔ IsColimiting (j ≫ H) ((gluingCoconeRestrict j H).app (op ⦋0⦌) c)
